headline: High: ctx can read/write filesystem and use MCP/browser tooling, while dagster is non-networked and read-only, creating prompt-injection and data-handling risk mainly through ctx’s shared workspace and external APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx can observe Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and uses mcp/stdio plus filesystem access, so it can ingest content from shared workspaces or tool outputs. dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or file I/O surfaces, so the bridge is one-way through ctx rather than a mutual channel. This is plausible in default developer setups, but not proven by direct pair evidence.
conditions: IF ctx is configured to watch a shared workspace containing attacker-controlled files, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF dagster outputs are copied into ctx-managed files or MCP events, ctx may treat them as instructions.
mitigations: Restrict ctx to a dedicated workspace directory.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted file contents in ctx.
Require manual review before ctx acts on tool-output text.
Separate dagster artifacts from ctx-observed paths.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for watched events.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, harness records, and filesystem content, and it calls external APIs such as GitHub and Claude Code. dagster itself is read-only with no network egress, so the leakage path is primarily ctx exporting shared data rather than dagster exfiltrating it. The pair can expose sensitive workspace data in default developer workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the workspace observed by ctx, those contents can be sent to external APIs.
IF dagster artifacts are stored in the same directory ctx monitors, ctx may forward them to GitHub or Claude Code.
mitigations: Limit ctx to non-sensitive directories.
Block ctx from processing secrets-bearing files.
Use separate credentials for ctx API calls.
Review outbound destinations in ctx before enabling it.
requires-engineering: enforce content filters on uploads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write the filesystem and install packages, while dagster cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or execute shells. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is ctx acting on shared files that dagster only reads. No shared mutable resource is documented, so the conflict surface is small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory through an external orchestrator, ctx can overwrite files dagster expects to remain stable.
IF dagster is wrapped by another system that adds write privileges, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Make dagster inputs read-only.
Run ctx and dagster under different OS users.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can observe tool events and produce context that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, while dagster is an orchestrator that could consume generated artifacts. The pairwise pathway exists if dagster ingests ctx output without verification, but dagster’s own profile does not show action-taking authority or direct trust of ctx. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF dagster consumes ctx-generated files or metadata without validation, incorrect context can cascade into pipeline decisions.
IF ctx summarizes facts from logs and dagster uses those summaries as source-of-truth, downstream errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require schema validation on ctx outputs before dagster reads them.
Add a human approval step for high-impact pipeline changes.
Compare ctx summaries against raw source data.
Log provenance for every ctx-derived artifact.
requires-engineering: implement signed handoff records.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and unverified, but only ctx explicitly touches audit/runtime logs and external APIs; dagster lists no secrets handled, no residency constraints, and no retention policy. There is no documented compliance mismatch such as PHI, EU PII, or regulated data flow, so the risk is limited to generic logging/retention uncertainty rather than a concrete breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx-observed logs or files, retention and residency controls must be checked.
IF dagster is later configured to process PHI or EU PII, a compliance review is required before pairing.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ctx-observed paths.
Document retention settings for ctx logs.
Confirm dagster data classes before deployment.
Separate compliance-sensitive workloads from this pair.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data classes.
